d_preserved_statement: The reviewed mechanic (t5-hedged-evidence-scope, design review r3 PASS 86) is preserved exactly: the child confirms the status card, reports to school, then reads all 3 affected-party cards (見学先/バス/宿, displayed in a per-session randomized order) and contacts them via one-shot taps -- only the hotel card discloses a real time-sensitive consequence (dinner-service cutoff), so contacting it before the other two is the judgment this game asks for (src/q1/delayRecoverLogic.ts's contactOrderWins mirrors design-sim.mjs byte-for-byte). Once all 3 are contacted, school approval and sharing are each gated behind their own prerequisite (button disabled until the prior stage completes), closing the reverse-audit's select-all/free-reorder exploit structurally rather than just discouraging it. Gate H (onComplete only when contactOrderWins is true, onPartialComplete otherwise with an honestly distinct failure framing) and Gate G (non-scored reflection re-presenting all 3 contacts' original detail text read-only, continue button gated on a full reflection order being picked) are both implemented and verified via source-level regression checks. Browser-verified end-to-end: both the success path (hotel contacted first, 🎉-style celebratory framing) and the failure path (hotel contacted last, honest distinct framing + reflection screen with data re-presented and gated continue) render and behave correctly, including two deliberate rapid-batched-click regression tests (opening/contacting 2 cards in the same synchronous script call) that confirm the functional-updater state pattern used throughout (contact/openContact/toggleReflect all read from setState's prev, not the render-scope closure) correctly registers every action under React 18 automatic batching -- this specifically guards against the exact class of bug found and fixed in legacy-hotel-receive's implementation review r1.
